framing_issues.text: What's uncertain: Georgia Power says Staff's three guidelines "are not based on ..." It says they should be given no weight.
framing_issues.issue: Plan C's 'What's uncertain' holds an opposing party's sharpest attack, which is an argument rather than an uncertainty. Plan B's 'What's uncertain' lists redactions and the model-access dispute but not Staff's critique of Georgia Power's plan ('only a partial solution', 'undue complexity', P-082), which appears only in card 3. The two plans are treated unevenly.

framing_issues.text: PIA Staff: PSC staff assigned to evaluate the case "from the standpoint of promoting the public interest ..."
framing_issues.issue: Only PIA Staff gets a mission statement, and it uses 'public interest' language. The quote is accurate (P-006), but readers may give Staff's positions extra weight. Other parties get neutral descriptions. A short note that Staff is an advocate party in the case would balance it.

framing_issues.text: the size of the change rests on Staff's estimate alone
framing_issues.issue: Missing context about redactions. Georgia Power did estimate Option 2 (P-138, Attachment B), but the estimate is blacked out (P-140). 'Alone' suggests no other estimate exists, which goes against the page's own rule that a blacked-out number 'exists but is hidden' (line 168). The sentence also cites the Option 1 attachment (P-139) instead of P-140.

framing_issues.text: It said its split builds on PIA Staff's own peak-based showing in the fuel case ... GIPL's filed testimony also said pipeline space "is required to meet peak demand conditions."
framing_issues.issue: Card 3 lists support for Georgia Power's plan without each source's own qualifier. Staff says its fuel-case 1-CP was a summer peak used 'simply for illustration purposes' (P-145, shown only in card 4), and GIPL rejected the winter-peak split (P-101). As written, both read as closer to Georgia Power than they are.

framing_issues.text: Georgia Power's rebuttal says GIPL's witness later moved to an energy-based split.
framing_issues.issue: Caveats are uneven. Plan D (line 138) and card 5 (line 227) add 'we could not check this account', but card 4 uses the same unchecked Georgia Power account as support for Staff's plan with no caveat. P-154 itself says only that GIPL 'appeared to abandon' its position.

framing_issues.text: system lambda / capital substitution / under collected fuel balance / large-load cost model / winter CP (lines 115, 125, 131, 201, 214, 249, 250)
framing_issues.issue: These technical terms are not explained on the page or in the glossary. 'System lambda' gets only GAM's partial gloss, and 'capital substitution' is named but never defined. That conflicts with the grade 6-8 reading target.

framing_issues.text: It said it "has committed to protect existing customers from bearing any of the costs of adding these large customers."
framing_issues.issue: This quote comes from Georgia Power's direct testimony about large-load customers (P-054), but it sits under 'Who disagrees' in the card on other fuel-related costs. Readers will take it as Georgia Power's answer on those costs.

framing_issues.text: The yearly totals are public: about $741 million in 2023, $824 million in 2024 and $732 million in 2025.
framing_issues.issue: These totals cover every category left out of the credit in P-150, including take-or-pay energy costs and pipeline and storage fees covered in cards 2 to 5, not just the coal, overhead and similar items card 6 is about. Shown in card 6, they make that card's issue look much larger than it is. The 'only a portion' caveat does not say what the totals contain.

framing_issues.text: Which costs should count as fuel costs at all; this is mainly a question of how to define them.
framing_issues.issue: This frames the dispute in Staff's and GIPL's terms (which costs are 'fuel-related', P-089, P-106). Georgia Power's objection is about rate design: a marginal-cost rate is not meant to recover embedded costs (P-121).

framing_issues.text: fixed fuel costs that serve all customers
framing_issues.issue: The question builds in PIA Staff's premise (P-080), which Georgia Power (P-130) and GIPL (P-100) dispute for take-or-pay contracts.
